Game is unfortunately buggy as fk still, and I'm kinda mad that it even made it out of early access when it is VERY broken still. I honestly do not understand how the devs agreed to fully release this game with broken mechanics and unfinished storyline as well. As if writing it's ver 1.2b-1246, but on the 1.0 release, there was still bugs such as the game being unable to recognise the player is some minigames, where you somehow are able to "interact" such as the hackysack in CherryBlossom Event, but the screen will not move as the player is actually not there, and the game will just crash because technically the player wasn't there.

There were also lots of graphical bugs such as being unable to see Tiles on the farm, like literally zero tiles were able to be seen yet it is actually there, I am able to remove it and put it back but unable to see it. (I put tiles on the farmland to prevent debris from coming back). In multiplayer as well you can't see any of the tiles and this issue dates BEFORE v1.2b. There is also an issue with Solar Orbs that are needed to progress with cleaning up the ocean floor, I started a new save, cleared the entire area that's relative to the nodes/altars, and the Orbs are NOWHERE to be seen and even passing by a WEEK in game. the Orb was still not spawning.

I understand that the devs put in a lot of effort into this game and honestly, I really love it. The style, the atmosphere, the story, the characters, they're all actually really really well done, but the mechanical and technical side of this game is extremely bad and felt as if the release was rushed (considering that the story wasn't even done in 1.0) and all these issues (while claimed to be "acknowledge") are just really really making the experience overrall bad. I'd have to give it a 5/10 on overrall experience. I just wish this was properly developed, properly loved, and not rushed for release.

reviews.review:
While the visuals are beautiful, the game is incredibly laggy at times. There's a reason for loading screens, and I wish the world was divided into multiple different parts with a loading screen in between, like Stardew Valley. I also think there's too much thrown at the player early on, everything is unlocked in the first week. While I usually don't mind that, this game has *so* much more to do than games in the same genre. It's overwhelming, the pacing could be better. Personally, the camera angle isn't my favorite either. Especially when mining, it can be hard to see where exactly you're hitting, and you lose energy because of it. 

When it comes to the festivals, the idea of them is nice, and I do like how interactive they are, but holy hell, those damn minigames. They're impossible to beat, even if you get everything perfect, make no mistakes, you still get last place! I especially dislike their difficulty because you miss out on rewards because of it. Plus, the game is advertised as a cozy game. There is nothing cozy about those damn festival minigames. 

When it comes to the characters, I do love them, the designs are great, but some of the cutscenes are so bland. Take Mark, for example. I love Mark, but he changed so fast. At first, he didn't like the farmer, then, one cutscene later, we're suddenly friendly? Plus, none of his cutscenes are about bonding with him, they're all about his relationship with his dog. Nothing related to the farmer and Mark's relationship. I think the non-friendable npcs are a problem too ("extras", I believe), they simply add nothing to the game. Why add a character if they're not even friendable? It's a waste of time, if you ask me, time that could be spent refining other parts of the game. 

I love the idea of the game, but I simply think it's too big, too much, too many things to keep track of. For example, there's way too many fishing locations to keep track of, the map is big and can be hard to navigate, there's so many npcs to keep track of, so many different skills to build, so many different things to complete (the temple, the ocean, quests, the cave, upgrading tools, building your farm, taking care of animals) and all of them take a lot of time. On top of all the earlier stuff, this game is filled with bugs. One simple thing (that you'd think wouldn't be a problem): eating food. Sometimes the game refuses to let you replenish your energy by eating food, and you're stuck with no energy the rest of the day.  

I think this game could absolutely be improved, they things mentioned above can be refined, which the developers have done with things! The combat used to be very clunky and awkward, but it no longer is, it is refined. I think with proper care and communication with the community, this game could be great. In a way, it already is. It has unique concepts that I like (like the underwater farming and the merpeople), but all in all I don't think this game is worth the price. Get Stardew Valley, it's actually worth the cost.
reviews.developer_response:
Hello,
Thank you for taking the time to write such a detailed and thoughtful review. We are sorry to hear the game has not fully lived up to your expectations, and we genuinely appreciate that you care enough about what it could be to share all of this.

Regarding the lag, we are actively gathering reports to help us investigate further. If you are open to it, could you please reach out to us at support@stairwaygames.com with your system specs? This will help us get a clearer picture of what might be contributing to it on your end.

On the food not replenishing energy - thank you for flagging that. If you can share any details on when it happened, such as which food item or what you were doing at the time, that would be really helpful for the team to track it down.

As for the feedback on pacing, the camera angle in the mines, festival minigame difficulty, character arcs, and the overall scope of the game, we will make sure all of it reaches the team. 

Thank you again for the feedback and understanding.

reviews.review:
I had more hours into early release when it was Game Pass, and I thought to tap into it again recently. I appreaciate the devs supporting the game with more and more updates almost 3 years in. when the game launched as 1.0 i remember players criticizing the state of the game as "unfinished".

I really wanted to love this game, I've tried to get into it multiple times, but it just never stucked into me like Stardew or A newer release like field of mistria. The game had a really nice premise, 3D style farm sim that ties into Indonesian culture. The art is great but the game itself just feels like it doesn't have that sauce that other farm sims had. 

One of the things I was always confused with was the narrative, they really dont know what they wanted to potray with this game. so the town is down under, low tourism and apparently on the lowest of the ranks. but they have a fancy lab, resort, hot springs, ,most of the town feels modern and so freaking clean other than the oil spill. and i dont wanna disrespect kickstarter backers but the whole quest of making this fancy "museum" even though the town is supposedly on crisis? it breaks the fourth wall too much in my opinion. 

The movement feels clunky and slow, even if the map is almost seamless with no loading screens. you gotta dash into everywhere and the only saving grace is the teleport function helping fairly early into the game. The gameplay is what you expected from a farming sim but somehow the game made it feel bland. particularly mining and diving was tedious without upgrading tools, and then just grindy and boring when you do upgrade tools. the lab upgrades are interesting but farming and ranching really didnt stand out to me that much. 

The 2D artstyle is good, but i have qualms about the 3D models integration into the game, it feels very bland and greyed out, some things feels disproportionate. the 3D artstyle really didnt benefit much from the top down perspective.

its just something that i feel like didnt fit really well. I love the character designs but story wise it didn't feel like anyone hit the mark with me in my playthroughs.

All in all the game is fine, scoring wise i'd say a good 7 out of 10. there's a lot of people that like this game, so it might not just be the one for me. I can see the art and goods of it but the feeling i get was bland

Ehhhhhh.

I played a lot of this game, and it's not that I didn't enjoy it, exactly, but... I walked away feeling rather disappointed, I guess.

There's a lot of interesting stuff going on with it, really there is- the setting itself is doing a lot of lifting here, and there are a lot of good quality of life inclusions I'm quite pleased about.

But it's all just so terribly vapid. Character events are delivered flatly and toothlessly, with no emotional heft at all. The characters themselves are broadly uninteresting. And to top it all off, the game is terribly grindy and awfully demanding of your time and effort- you spend a lot of time blitzing around desperately trying to get everything done in a day and still make some kind of progress on your larger goals. I'm not sure what it is that makes this feel so pronounced in this game specifically when time pressure is a standard element of the genre, but it feels tyrannical rather than gently urgent.

I guess the problem is that there are just better farming sims with more personality, stronger identities, and more sincerity and heart. This game is fine... but it's merely fine, in a genre that contains greatness.

reviews.review: No local co-op despite being a part of the initial early-access roadmap and features.

I wanted to like this game because so many people seemed to enjoy it.  However, the ripping off of Stardew Valley is so evident in every detail of the game.  The story is so similar that's impossible not to see.  Even some of the art for certain characters is almost exact.  I think the main reason why people like this game is because it's graphics are more palatable  If you want to play Stardew I suggest you play Stardew rather than this knock off.

The developers have put a lot into this game, and the things to do in it is probably unrivalled in the cozy farming sim category, but I can't in any good  faith recommend the game. 

It has a variety of bugs and issues, many dating back to early release that the developers just seem completely oblivious or indifferent to, just answering any concerns with a standard copy and paste "We're aware of the issue" rubber stamp response to any issue old and new.

The stamina fruit bug has been there since release. Thank goodness I read the forums and knew of this bug existing. Bought the stamina fruit from the ship at the lighthouse. Character automatically ate it and it immediately disabled all player input. Wouldn't accept input from controller, mouse, or keyboard.

Had to leave the game running, and walk away from the computer until the day timed out until the next morning. Luckily the ship only appears after 8pm at night, so didn't lose much playtime. But many players end up exiting their game because of the stamina/wellness fruit bug and lose a  whole day's work. Even those players who know it's been a issue since release are stuck waiting up to 30 minutes or so, waiting their frozen game to time out for the day so that they can be penalized, teleported home, and lose out the rest of the day just to get input controls back.

It's a serious issue since those permanent stat increasing items are pretty much the grand rewards to major quest lines...but the actual reward seems to be designed to ruin everyone's gaming experience and lock you out of your computer for awhile.

Funny but sad in a way too, sine the standard response from the devs over the years has been to send them the affected save file so that they can see what's going on in, obviously, their spare time but if the bug triggers you have to wait til the game day times out to get control of your game, but of course each new day reactivates input controls and overwrites the affected save file.

In any case, I would never recommend any game here that I wouldn't recommend to personal family or friends, and until the devs actually consider serious issues with their game as more than just a glance in their rear view mirror, I can't recommend it. It  has a lot to offer, but the foundation is cracked, and the door tends to jam, locking  you out rather than let you in to play.
reviews.developer_response:
Hi RCJenn,

Thank you for taking the time to write such a detailed review. We want you to know that we read every word of it, and we hear you.

We want to address a few of your points directly:

- The Stamina Fruit Bug: You’re right; this has been one of our most stubborn issues. A fix was included in our previous patch, but unfortunately, the issue is still occurring in some cases. We are still actively gathering information to implement a more permanent fix. We also want to thank you for your willingness to help us through the Steam forum discussion.

- The Save File Request: We ask for these because the bug appears to be tied to specific save data and game progress rather than a universal trigger. That said, we completely understand how frustrating our communication around this has been, and we will do our best to improve our process going forward.

We genuinely appreciate that you love what this game has to offer, and we are sorry the experience has let you down. Thank you again for your understanding and feedback.

I would recommend Coral Island mainly to players who have never played Stardew Valley, because to me it feels very much like a copy rather than a truly original experience. While the game does introduce some new features… like the underwater world, which is a nice idea… it still struggles to stand out.

The graphics are another weak point for me. I personally find the character designs quite unattractive, and overall the visual style feels a bit cheap rather than polished or immersive. Because of that, I find it hard to really get drawn into the game.

I’ve actually tried playing it twice, but each time I couldn’t fully get into it. It just doesn’t have the same charm or uniqueness that Stardew Valley has. That game sets such a high standard that Coral Island ends up feeling like a weaker version in comparison.

That said, I might give it another chance in the future. And to be fair, I think it could still appeal to players who are looking for a cozy farming game and aren’t too demanding when it comes to graphics… especially if they haven’t experienced Stardew Valley before.

I can still appreciate that the game has some potential, but personally I wouldn’t recommend it. Having already played Stardew Valley, it’s hard for me to enjoy Coral Island because the similarities are just too strong. It ends up feeling extremely similar, and that comparison kind of ruins the experience for me.

Am I interested in the characters around me? Not at all

reviews.review:
I've put a lot of hours into this game at launch, and at 2 points since then. Probably around 200 hours, taking into account my bad habit of leaving games running overnight.

At it's core, Coral Island is a competent cozy farming / life sim game. It has most of the genre staples and a few minor unique twists. The character art is gorgeous, even if it doesn't quite translate to the 3D models.

However, the game launched in a relatively incomplete state, taking ages until patch 1.1 brought the game to its promised launch state, and at 2.5 years post launch we're still waiting without end for patch 1.3 to actually deliver on all their post launch promises. And when each patch launches, you bet it's going to be full of bugs, only some of which will get fixed. 

[h2] Positive [/h2]
[list]
    [*] Simple but beautiful graphics
    [*] Fairly undemanding game, got it running even on my old PC with a gtx 970
    [*] Good character variety
    [*] A good breadth of activities - the diving element helps distinguish Coral Island from being a complete SD clone. 
[/list]

[h2] Negative [/h2]
[list]
    [*] Repetitive Dialogue
    [*] Slow, clunky animations
    [*] Frequent bugs, sometimes gamebreaking
    [*] Very slow update cadence, including for bug fixes
    [*] Limited house customisation - your house even with all the furniture you can make/buy looks incredibly bare compared to NPC houses, especially with this style of graphics. 
[/list]

Honestly, I almost gave this game a positive review, but until 1.3 is out and the devs manage to make this game relatively bug free, I can't in good conscience do that.
reviews.developer_response:
Hello,
Thank you for the detailed and honest review, and for the 200 hours you have put into the game. 

We are sorry to hear that bugs, repetitive dialogue, and clunky animations have gotten in the way of your experience. We would love to look into the specific issues you encountered further. 

If you are open to it, could you please share the details at support@stairwaygames.com - such as which dialogues felt repetitive, which animations felt off, and any game-breaking bugs you ran into, along with what you were doing in-game when they occurred? We'll do our best to investigate your case thoroughly with the team. 

We also appreciate the feedback on house customisation, and will make sure to relay it to the team. We are currently working on the 1.3 release and are hopeful that the improvements we have made will be worth your wait.

Thanks again for your understanding and for taking the time to share your thoughts.

reviews.review: The game is cute, nice art and I like the idea of trying to clean up the enviroment and all that but the gameplay is extremely grindy, slow and clunky. Just like all the stardew clones it has the farm, the mines and the villiage. This game also includes an underwater diving system where you dive anderwater and slowly swim around an area breaking down trash. Both the mines and the Diving feel indestinguishable from eachother as really they are both just clicking on and breaking either rocks or trash with a very clunky and simple combat system thrown in just because. Maybe other people will enjoy it for the grind but with nothing more than generic farming mechanics and grindy mine clones it's only redeeming feature in my eyes is the game looks pretty. The art, models and UI look great (to me) but overall very underwhealming. I personally can't bring myself to sink in the hours doing the same very, very basic tasks to grind the reasources to upgrade the seeds and machines but if you enjoy turning your brain off to click the same 4 variations of either sea trash or stones till you run out of energy maybe you'll enjoy this game. Okay, I wanted to like this game—I really did. The island and the characters were obviously designed with a lot of love and attention to detail. There's real passion and talent here. My problem is that the game just... plays poorly. The movements are slow and fiddly, there's this weird little sprint that the player can do (which for some reason isn't possible in the mines), and the animations feel very slow and clunky. This was exacerbated during all of the combat in the game. One of the reasons I think Stardew Valley is so successful is that the animations are crisp and satisfying, so the mundane, button-mashing chores in the game like chopping wood and harvesting crops still feel good. Harvesting crops doesn't feel good in Coral Island.

The game also has some performance issues and is often laggy, which doesn't exactly improve the problems mentioned above.

UPDATE: I got the game to work by switching from my PC with dedicated graphics card and 16gb RAM  to my Macbook pro M4 chip with integrated graphics card and 16g RAM. There is no reason this should work but it does. I tried parallels, boosteroid, porting kit, and crossover and found crossover to have the best function for running the game. Parallels did not work, porting kit did not work, and boosteroid worked with subpar performance and more lag. So far no crashes on my Macbook just some lag in more dense game areas. Hope this info helps some of you!

Genuinely unplayable.

Got this game on sale and was very excited to play it as I have been following for years. When trying to run it (on a computer that can comfortably run games with much higher requirements) I only get one of two results: either unreal engine immediately crashes and crashes the game or I make it to starting a new game and the screen is just black outside of the basic UI elements. I spent a lot of time trying to workshop the issues and reading forums while waiting to see if the graphics would finally load so of course my refund request was denied due to racking up play time. From what I've read in the forums, the crashing is constant, worse than it was in the past, AND the game that has crashing issues has NO manual save options so when it crashes those that are lucky enough to be able to actually play the game lose all their progress for the day. I haven't been able to try any fixes for the issues because the devs only response to any issues seems to be telling people to email them the crash log and system specs and there's no tips anywhere for what could be wrong. Oh and if you have an integrated graphics card apparently you cannot run the game.

I would say absolutely do not pay full price for this game, and wait until they implement manual saving to buy it at all. And if you experience crashing issues within the first hour just quit while you're ahead and request a refund so you won't get denied. I have never experienced a game this unplayable in my life.
reviews.developer_response:

Thank you for taking the time to leave a review, and we are truly sorry to hear about the experience you have had.

We want to address your specific concerns directly to provide some clarity:

Integrated Graphics & Black Screens: Our minimum requirements specify a dedicated GPU (Nvidia GeForce GTX 660 2GB or equivalent). Most integrated graphics chips struggle to render the game's assets, which is likely the cause of the black screen and immediate Unreal Engine crashes you're seeing.

Manual Saving: We hear you loud and clear. Losing a full day of progress to a crash is incredibly disheartening. Our development team is actively working on implementing it, with plans to include it in the upcoming 1.3 update. For more details, feel free to check our latest dev blog here: https://blog.stairwaygames.com/post/1-million-units-full-crossplay-roadmap

Why we ask for logs: We know it feels repetitive to be told to "email us," but because Unreal Engine crashes can be caused by anything from hardware conflicts to driver versions, those crash logs are the only way our engineers can 'see' exactly where the code failed on your specific machine.

If you are still open to it, please reach out to support@stairwaygames.com. We will look into why the game fails to run smoothly for you.

Thank you for the years you've followed our journey, and thank you for your understanding.

Updated review after ~70 hours

It's OK, just has no wow factor, like Sandrock.

The atmosphere isn't great, the social is so dull it's tempting to just skip and get on with the grind.  I have heard people say "it lacks soul" and I agree with that.  The social also seems to have little impact on the game, and they don't talk about any specific event or shared challenge, just boring ♥♥♥♥ about their life that is painful to sit through.

It's pretty, and what is there of the UI is good, but missing huge amounts of QOL and UI screens needed for tracking 10s of items.  

Towards the end game, the amount of missing QOL is infuriating.  Even things like the second-long UI fade in / out are pissing me off and slowing me down that I probably won't finish it.  And why can't I see the price of an item when I hover unless it's at the point of sale?  If you want to make us open and close inventory screens non-stop get rid of the fade delay.

Also I'm not usually a fan of them, but I personally think the game is begging for quest arrows.  Or at least show the icon of the item you need to give so you don't have to Google everything.  After 60 hours I still run into the wrong alley and get lost sometimes.  It's pretty, just not memorable.

Fix the QOL.

Because it's a satisfying, well polished grind. 



==  Previous review @ ~5 hours

Hate to say it but I am going to be that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and give this a red for the save system.

The lack of quick save is a dealer breaker for me.  I like to play at my own time, not in 20 minute blocks.  I am 3 hours in and can't get past this issue.  I may persist,  or I may return when v 1.3 is done.  

That's why I can't recommend it because I think a lot of people would get pissed off by that archaic game design.

But, it seems good.  Incredibly clean UI, hotbar, clear data.  Not sure about the overall feel and look of the characters - this definitely falls short of Sandrock in terms of atmosphere.  

Just add the save system pls devs...
